text:
Artemi Panarin has been away from the Kings lately, missing games for family reasons (Daily Faceoff) and not with the team to begin a road trip (CBS Sports). His last game was Nov. 12. That matters more than any number here.

When he plays, the 35-year-old is still the engine. He has 19 points in 17 games, and Los Angeles has taken 61% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 16 points better than without him. The odd part is the scoring: the Kings have scored 9.9 fewer goals than those chances deserve with him out there, which has cost him points. That kind of gap usually swings back.

He's on his fourth NHL team after Chicago, Columbus and the Rangers, and never was drafted, coming over from the KHL. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the league's better setup men last season (9.5 primary shot assists per 60, 91st percentile among forwards), and Evolving-Hockey put him at 2.8 wins above replacement. When he's back, the production should start to match the play.
headline: Panarin's points are lagging his play
